verdicts.reason: All rules hold: a jq exit code enforces one frame, one string subject and a numeric score; status is assisted as the brief rates it; an unscored null is a valid result; and checkRunnable is false.

All rules hold: one exit code requires exactly one file (frame_t.png) and a cmp match to the brief's reference frame at t; a missing reference counts as unchecked and a renderer that is not a function of t counts as unsupported; status is assisted; checkRunnable is false because the harness does not exist.

All rules hold: one program counts changed frames (exactly the worst one), requires its rescore, and blocks render_started below the threshold; a below-threshold or unscored result is valid; status is assisted; checkRunnable is false because no such program exists yet.

All rules hold: a jq exit code enforces the mesh, UV, rig, animation order, the default rig, exactly one animation, no import and no level placement; a partial manifest of earlier stages is valid; status is assisted; checkRunnable is false.

A3 fails: the done-when gates only on the one-class diff, while the editor validation is only quoted separately and nothing requires a revert when the path breaks, so two elements of the brief's definition are not enforced.

A3 fails: the done-when enforces read-before-write, the named system and an edit confined to it, but the brief's 'walk the path after' is never asserted (it is always reported 'not run'), so one element of the brief's definition is not enforced.
